stages.headline: The area of a sphere is S = 4πR², four times the area of a great disc.
stages.headlineEnglish: The area of a sphere is S = 4πR², four times the area of a great disc.

stages.headline: Example: R = 3 gives S = 36π; doubling the radius makes the area 4 times larger.
stages.headlineEnglish: Example: R = 3 gives S = 36π; doubling the radius makes the area 4 times larger.

stages.headline: The area of a sphere equals the lateral area of the circumscribed cylinder: 2πR · 2R = 4πR² (Archimedes).
stages.headlineEnglish: The area of a sphere equals the lateral area of the circumscribed cylinder: 2πR · 2R = 4πR² (Archimedes).
